title: mitigate-prefetch-race-in-continuous-batcher-causing-intermittent-tail-latency
creator: Asha Menon
description: Multiple paid customers (enterprise support tickets #SC-4491, #SC-4522) reported intermittent 95/99th percentile generation latency spikes originating during mixed-length microbursts on the continuous batcher. The root reproducible condition is an interleaved prefetch + admission race that temporarily holds the KV-cache mutex while prefetching evictions, which blocks short-latency requests and amplifies long-context tail latency across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket tracks the investigation, fix, rollout strategy, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
symptoms:
- Short requests (<=128 tokens) observe 5x higher p95/p99 for up to 2-5s during node-local microbursts
- Observed on both hosted and dedicated nodes; Private customer reported similar pattern after upgrade to runtime-1.20
- Metrics: sudden spike in kv_cache_mutation_lock_hold_seconds, dispatcher_queue_depth, and a correlated drop in small-batch throughput
- Alerts triggered: svc/latency-95 exceeding SLO for customers with latency SLOs
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy synthetic traffic generator with mixed-length mix (80% small, 20% long) and microburst pattern (200 concurrent small requests over 200ms)
2) Enable continuous batching and KV prefetch on target node
3) Observe scheduler traces and kv_cache lock hold metrics; reproduce tail spikes in p95/p99
4) Use flamegraphs and pprof to capture the prefetch path and admission path overlap
investigation_notes:
2026-02-28: Slack escalation from support (private-cust-7) with p99 traces attached.
2026-03-01: Reproduced locally using synthetic workload; confirmed extended mutex hold in kv cache prefetch path.
2026-03-03: Found race: prefetch evict+load path grabs cache mutex and initiates background IO; admission threads waiting to acquire same mutex for quick KV hits are blocked.
2026-03-05: Verified hypothesis on dedicated pool; replicated on Private VPC after customer upgrade.
2026-03-07: Benchmarked three mitigation approaches: 1) finer-grained locks on cache shards, 2) optimistic prefetch with try-lock fallback, 3) offboard prefetch to separate worker thread with admission token. Try-lock fallback had lowest code surface risk but marginally higher eviction rate.
2026-03-09: Decided on combination: optimistic try-lock + offboard worker for heavy prefetch, with metrics and guardrails.
2026-03-11: Implementation branch created and reviewed (GH: redwood-inference/runtime#1456).
design_decisions:
- Do not convert to full fine-grained per-bucket locks (large refactor, higher risk).
- Implement try-lock on hot path: if prefetch cannot acquire lock within 2ms, enqueue prefetch request to a dedicated prefetch worker to avoid blocking admission.
- Add admission fast-path that avoids cache mutation locks for pure GET hits.
- Expose new runtime metric: prefetch_offboard_count and prefetch_trylock_failures.
- Default prefetch offboard enabled for hosted; config flag for Dedicated/Private to allow controlled rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- No p99 latency regressions in mixed-length microburst synthetic tests across three hardware profiles.
- kv_cache_mutation_lock_hold_seconds 90th drops by >=70% under test pattern.
- New metrics (prefetch_offboard_count, trylock_failures) emit and are wired to dashboards.
- Automated regression test added to e2e suite that simulates microburst.
- Rollout plan and feature flag exist for Dedicated and Private customers.

rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (hosted): enable default in runtime-1.21 with canary rollout to 5% of host pool for 48h, monitor prefetch_trylock_failures, prefetch_offboard_count, kv_cache_lock_hold_seconds, and customer SLOs.
Phase 2 (dedicated): opt-in configuration per tenant; coordinate with Success for tenants with SLOs and schedule maintenance.
Phase 3 (private): ship as configurable toggle in operator manifests; notify customers and offer assisted upgrade.
Rollback: toggle off feature flag and revert to prior runtime build; ensure transient metric thresholds for automated rollback.
test_plan:
- Add unit tests for try-lock path and offboard queue behavior.
- Add e2e scenario in perf-cicd that replays mixed-length microburst for 1M requests.
- Run canary perf tests across curated hardware profiles (A10032GB, T4, L4x8).
qa_notes: QA to validate: feature flag toggles, metrics emitted, offboard queue bounds enforce backpressure, no deadlocks introduced. Re-run customer repro scenario using their traffic capture (S3: s3://private-cust-7/traces/2026-02-27).

- 2026-03-02: Notified affected customers with interim mitigation (increase small-request concurrency limits and temporary admission prioritization).
- 2026-03-12: Shared planned fix and ETA (runtime-1.21 canary 3/14); scheduled customer-facing status update and optional private patch for on-prem installations.
follow_ups:
- Add regression alarm tied to trylock_failures > threshold and sustained p99 increase.
- Investigate long-term design: evaluate per-shard cache with read-copy-update for admission fast-path.
- Post-rollout: run 30d rolling analysis to ensure no recurrence.
- Update runbook for on-call with clear triage steps and quick remediation playbook.
